title: Design: rate limiter class
objective: Turn the token bucket into a clean class: one bucket per user, and a clock passed in so tests don't have to wait.

sources.title: Robert C. Martin, Solid Relevance (Clean Coder Blog, 2020): one-line definitions of all five SOLID principles

simplifies: Buckets live in one process's memory and are never cleaned up. Real limiters share state across servers (often in Redis), expire idle users' buckets, and tell clients when to retry.

exercise.change: Log every blocked request, with the user and the time.
exercise.hint: Each class counts requests in its own way. Where is the decision to block made?

options.text: Put the limiting in one Limiter class (per-user buckets, a clock passed in) that all three use
options.explanation: Right. The block decision happens in one place, so logging it is one edit.

options.text: Add a log line to each class's own counting code
options.explanation: Three edits, and three slightly different limiters to keep in step.
Login is where limits matter most: it slows password guessing.

exercise.explain: Gateway, Login and Upload ask Limiter.allow(user). The decision is made in one place, so logging blocked requests is one edit, and the fake clock makes it easy to test.

quiz.prompt: Why pass a clock into the Limiter instead of calling time.time() inside it?

options.text: Tests can use a fake clock and run a minute of traffic instantly, with exact times
options.explanation: Right. Hidden calls to the real clock make tests slow and flaky.
It's accurate enough; the problem is testing.

options.text: Python doesn't allow time.time() in classes
options.explanation: It does; passing the clock in is a design choice.

quiz.prompt: Asha has used all her tokens. Ravi sends his first request. What happens?

options.text: It's allowed: Ravi has his own bucket
options.explanation: Right. Per-user buckets stop one busy user from blocking everyone.

options.text: It's blocked: the limiter is out of tokens
options.explanation: Tokens are per user here, not shared.

options.text: It waits until Asha's bucket refills
options.explanation: Ravi's request doesn't depend on Asha's bucket at all.
